transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Sable - Head of ML), Raj Patel (Sable - CTO), Erin Lopez (Sable - Platform Engineer), Samir Gomez (Sable - Security)

Summary:
Quick quarterly health check / QBR to review usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents from last quarter, and roadmap alignment. Main asks from Sable: better cost projection for seasonal spikes, clarification on data residency + KMS options for Private deployment, and a short benchmark for their 512-token median calls to evaluate Dedicated vs Hosted economics.

Topics:
- Usage & cost trends
- Reliability and incident review (Jan outage, degraded throughput)
- Dedicated vs hosted decision criteria
- Security & compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML)
- Roadmap and next 90 days (pilot, benchmarks, procurement)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Romero: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We wanted to do a quick QBR style health check, go over metrics, cost, and any open items. Priya and Jordan are with me from Redwood. Maya, Raj, Erin, Samir, great to see you.

[00:00:18] Maya Chen: Thanks Alex, yeah thanks for setting this up, busy quarter for us but excited to sync.

[00:00:27] Raj Patel: Quick note, we'll probably have to run a short procurement check later — timeline is tight for us.

[00:00:35] Jordan Lee: Noted, Raj. We'll make sure to highlight the procurement next steps.

[00:00:42] Priya Nair: I can start with the reliability recap — last quarter we saw a single degraded throughput event on Jan 12th where latency increased ~2x for about 45 minutes, triggered by a sudden prefix storm on one of the public models. We rolled a fallback to a lower-latency variant and KV cache warm up helped recovery. The incident postmortem is in the shared doc: link: https://redwood.app/incident-jan12 (note: placeholder link).

[00:01:10] Erin Lopez: Yeah we saw increased 503s for a bit, our team opened a ticket with support. The retry guidance helped but we lost some early-morning traffic.

[00:01:22] Priya Nair: Right, and for Sable specifically we had region routing to avoid the hot-spot and later adjusted batching config. The config we applied reduced p95 by about 120 ms on average.

[00:01:36] Maya Chen: That aligns with our metrics. Looking at tokens, most of our calls are short-ish — median around 512 tokens — but we do have a small tail of long sessions at checkout flows.

[00:01:47] Alex Romero: Ok good context. On costs: Jordan, do you want to run through the usage / cost trends?

[00:01:55] Jordan Lee: Sure. So Sable spiked in January — token consumption up 42% month-over-month due to holiday promos. Your unit costs on the hosted plan are still materially lower than self-hosting given your current footprint, but the Dedicated reserved proposal we sent can reduce unit price by ~18% if you commit to the 6-month baseline. I'll attach the updated price sheet.

[00:02:17] Raj Patel: We're evaluating that — our main concern is burst capacity during promos. Would we lose burst flexibility if we go Dedicated?

[00:02:24] Priya Nair: No — Dedicated supports burst pools and autoscaling policies. You can configure burst lanes to use shared capacity for unexpected spikes. There's a trade-off: Reserved baseline gives predictability and lower unit cost, but if you overshoot baseline often then the marginal costs on burst capacity scale differently.

[00:02:44] Maya Chen: Do you have an example runbook for autoscaling and burst thresholds? That would help our SREs.

[00:02:50] Priya Nair: Yes, Priya: I mean, Jordan has a standard autoscale template, I'll send it — sorry brain slip — the template includes thresholds, cooldown windows, and a sample policy tuned for retail seasonality.

[00:03:06] Jordan Lee: I'll share that after the call.

[00:03:12] Raj Patel: On security: Samir — he has questions about KMS keys and data residency — can you summarize?

[00:03:18] Samir Gomez: Yeah, main ask is we need customer-managed keys in a specific AWS region, and our compliance team wants to confirm that logs/audit trails are retained for 13 months and that we can pull a full request trace. Also SSO via SAML and RBAC restrictions for non-prod vs prod.

[00:03:36] Alex Romero: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and can do region-coded keys; for hosted we have managed KMS but enterprise private offers customer-managed keys. Jordan — I can send the SOC 2 artifact and the KMS integration guide.

[00:03:49] Jordan Lee: Yep, I'll attach SOC2, ISO summary, and the audit log export guide. Expect an email with links by EOD.

[00:03:58] Maya Chen: Great — that will help. Also, for the proof point on latency if we try Dedicated, can Redwood run a short benchmark simulating our median 512-token workload? We'd like to see p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens across hosted vs dedicated.

[00:04:14] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll do a benchmark on a similar model variant and with your batching profile. Quick Q: do you use streaming for the majority of calls?

[00:04:22] Maya Chen: About 60% streaming, but the checkout sessions are non-streaming because of structured output.

[00:04:27] Priya Nair: Ok good to know, we'll include streaming vs non-streaming tests.

[00:04:33] Raj Patel: Also curious on quantization options; we've read Redwood Optimize suggests 8-bit quant for some models — what's the quality trade-off?

[00:04:41] Priya Nair: For many decoder-only models 8-bit quantization with calibration can give 20-30% drop in memory and similar latency improvements, with negligible quality loss for standard prompts. For more sensitive structured outputs you might want to test an eval set. We can pair the benchmark with a quick quality-regression eval on a set of 20 prompts from you.

[00:05:00] Erin Lopez: I'll prepare 20 prompts and expected outputs and drop them in the shared folder.

[00:05:05] Maya Chen: Thanks, Erin. On the procurement path, Raj — is legal ready to engage or do they need the compliance packet first?

[00:05:12] Raj Patel: They'll need the compliance packet, plus our procurement team wants an initial SOW estimate. We have an internal review 3/18, so if we can get materials by next week that'd be ideal.

[00:05:24] Alex Romero: Ok we can target getting the compliance packet and pricing breakdown by Friday 3/6. Jordan will send the SOW estimate.

[00:05:32] Jordan Lee: I'll draft a 6-month SOW with the dedicated baseline and burst notes and share as a Google doc.

[00:05:40] Samir Gomez: One note on audit logs — can we get near-real-time access or will we have to pull exports? Our SIEM ingests logs hourly.

[00:05:47] Jordan Lee: We can deliver a log forwarding integration to your SIEM via S3 or an HTTP endpoint; hourly export is default but we can set up streaming for event types you care about. I'll include config options in the security doc.

[00:06:02] Maya Chen: Back to costs quickly — is there a recommended approach for selecting model catalog entries? We saw multiple variants with different perf/cost tradeoffs.

[00:06:10] Priya Nair: We typically advise matching to your success criteria: latency SLO -> choose low-latency variant; cost prioritization -> choose quantized or distilled variants. We also provide per-route routing so you can route checkout to low-latency model and marketing summaries to a cheaper variant.

[00:06:26] Raj Patel: Route-based SLAs sound promising. Do we get per-route cost and token-level breakdowns in the console?

[00:06:32] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token breakdown, and trace links. We can give a short demo of the console analytics if you'd like.

[00:06:40] Maya Chen: Let's do a focused console demo in the next call — maybe include billing and token-level views.

[00:06:46] Alex Romero: Sounds good. I'll put that on the follow-up.

[00:06:50] Priya Nair: For the benchmark logistics, can someone drop a minimal example of the typical payload and a short token distribution? It doesn't need to be PII.

[00:06:58] Erin Lopez: I'll drop a sanitized sample and distribution CSV by end of day tomorrow.

[00:07:05] Maya Chen: And one operational question — we saw a guidance note about KV cache persistence; our engineers asked whether the KV cache survives container restarts in private deployments.

[00:07:14] Priya Nair: In Private, KV cache persistence depends on the runtime mode. For Stateful mode it persists across restarts; for stateless scaled pods the runtime will rebuild caches. We'll include specifics for your on-prem topology in the security / deployment doc.

[00:07:30] Samir Gomez: That helps. Any network requirements for on-prem? We'll need firewall rules and IP ranges.

[00:07:36] Alex Romero: We'll include a network checklist with IP ranges and ports for the Private package.

[00:07:42] Raj Patel: Ok last thing — what's the usual SLA for failover in Dedicated? We want to understand RTOs for the primary pool.

[00:07:49] Jordan Lee: Our SLA for Dedicated is 99.95% with automated failover across pools; RTO for an automatic fallback to a compatible variant is typically under 2 minutes, but we can run a DR test during the pilot to validate.

[00:08:04] Maya Chen: Good to know.

[00:08:10] Alex Romero: Great — to recap: action items and next steps: Jordan to send pricing/SOW and SOC2 artifacts by 3/6; Priya to run benchmarks and prototype autoscale policy, Maya/Erin to supply token distribution and eval prompts; Jordan to schedule security deep-dive with Samir. We'll reconvene after the benchmark.

[00:08:32] Raj Patel: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.

[00:08:36] Alex Romero: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

[00:08:40] (call ends)

Notes/Links referenced: https://redwood.app/incident-jan12 (postmortem), pricing spreadsheet (internal link), SOC2 packet (will be attached), deployment/network checklist (will be attached).

Quality notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution slips, and a few technical terms transcribed incorrectly ("KV cash" for KV cache in one spot in the raw transcript).
